data <- tuesdata$vesuvius

EDA

dataF1 <- data %>% filter(event_id != is.na(event_id) & time != is.na(time) & latitude != is.na(latitude) & longitude != is.na(longitude) & depth_km != is.na(depth_km) & duration_magnitude_md != is.na(duration_magnitude_md) & md_error != is.na(md_error) & area != is.na(area) & type != is.na(type) & review_level != is.na(review_level) & review_level == 'preliminary' & year != is.na(year))

This is to see how many observations are complete.

For ease of exploration, I am going to continue with only the complete observations for now.

I may go back and perform final analysis and visualization on original dataset, but for now just complete observations

dataClean <- dataF1 %>% rename(Magnitude = duration_magnitude_md) %>% mutate(year = as_factor(year)) %>% select(time,latitude,longitude,depth_km,Magnitude,year)

I left out ‘event ID’ because it is a number that was assigned for data purposes

I left out ‘md_error’ because they are all the same

I left out ‘area’ because they are all the same

I left out ‘type’ because they are all the same

I left out ‘review_level’ because there are only two samples that are different

Hypothesis A: There will be a trend of earthquake magnitudes over time

Finding the avg magnitude for each year:

avgByYear <- dataClean %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(avg_magnitude = mean(Magnitude) , N = n() ) 
ggplot(avgByYear,aes(as.factor(year),avg_magnitude)) + geom_point()

I see no clear trend in the scatterplot

Hypothesis B: Each year will see a different average magnitude

I will need to conduct ANOVA to determine if it is valid to compare these means

I have to first create a dataframe for each year and analyze for ~ normality (I will only be using the years that have a large enough sample size to anlalyze)

Back to the ANOVA

anova_model <- aov(Magnitude ~ year, data = dataClean) 
summary(anova_model)

After some research, this tool does mean testing against all possible pairs of years
The result was that some years may have similar means, but overall most year pairs are different in mean magnitude.

PapaPlot <- ggplot(avgByYear , 
                   aes(x=as.factor(year) , 
                       y=avg_magnitude)) + 
  geom_col(aes(fill = as.factor(year))) + 
  geom_xsideviolin(data=dataClean, 
                   aes(x=year, 
                       y=Magnitude, 
                       fill = as.factor(year)), 
                   orientation = 'x' ) + 
  labs(title='Mount Vesuvius Earthquakes (2013-2024)' ,
       y='Average Magnitude' , 
       x='Year' , 
       fill = 'Year') + 
  theme_classic() + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d() + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5)) + 
  theme(ggside.panel.scale.x = .4)

print(PapaPlot)

This created a plot that shows the average eartquake magnitudes varying every year. I used the GGside to create a boxplot violin plot to show the distribution of each year. I believe this helps the audience understand that although the average magnitudes are different, all the years may not be completely normally distrbuted. I found that not all years are completely normally distributed during my EDA, but I still wanted to show the variances of the averages.
